name: TPMT (THIOPURINE METHYL TRANSFERASE) ENZYME ACTIVITY
interpretation:
The TPMT enzyme activity test measures an individual's ability to metabolize certain medications, especially thiopurine drugs like azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, and thioguanine.

  • TPMT levels below 5.5 Units indicate very low activity, suggesting a possible homozygous deficiency genomic type. This indicates a significantly impaired ability to metabolize thiopurine drugs, increasing the risk of severe adverse reactions. Alternative medications or reduced doses may be necessary.
  • Levels between 5.5 - 15.5 units indicate medium activity, possibly indicating a heterozygous deficiency type. Individuals with intermediate activity may still tolerate thiopurine drugs but may require dosage adjustments or closer monitoring to avoid toxicity or inadequate therapeutic response.
  • Levels above 15.5 Units indicate normal to high activity, possibly indicating a normal genomic type. Individuals with normal TPMT activity can metabolize thiopurine drugs effectively, leading to therapeutic drug levels in the bloodstream without excessive toxicity. However, very high activity may reduce drug efficacy, necessitating consideration of alternative medications.

Clinical Utility

  • TPMT Enzyme Activity (Thiopurine Methyl Transferase) testing is done before prescribing thiopurine drugs to identify patients at risk of hematopoietic toxicity and start them on a reduced dose or alternate therapy
  • About 89% of individuals have normal activity, 11% have intermediate activity, and 0.3% have low or undetectable activity.
